issues.legal_issue: The existing local tenant-protection order continued to govern execution until the general property law was extended to the state.
material_facts: The tenant-protection order of 1948 restricted eviction and required a certificate from the Controller before a civil-court eviction decree could be executed.
The general property law was extended to the state by notification with effect from a date after possession had been delivered.
The local tenant-protection order remained in force when the execution order was made and possession was delivered.
issues.conclusion: The tenant-protection order was an existing law saved by Article 372 of the Constitution and remained unaffected by Article 254; the claimed repugnancy did not arise.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that the Part B States (Laws) Act, 1951, did not itself bring the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, into force in the state; that required an extension by notification under section 3 of the Act. Until that extension took effect, the existing local order remained in force, was saved by Article 372, and was unaffected by Article 254. The court considered M/s. Tilakram Rambaksh v. Bank of Patiala.

predicates.execution_proceeding: A party seeks to enforce a civil-court decree through execution proceedings.
predicates.local_tenant_protection_in_force: A local law restricting eviction of tenants was in force when execution was sought.
predicates.general_property_law_not_yet_effective: The general property law had not yet taken effect in the relevant jurisdiction when execution was sought.

issues.definition: When execution is sought while local tenant protection is in force and the general property law is not yet effective, the local tenant protection governs execution.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant may challenge execution and obtain restoration of possession delivered under an ex parte order that contravened a statutory restriction on eviction.
material_facts: The tenant-protection order prohibited eviction in execution of a decree unless the required certificate had been obtained from the Controller.
The decree-holders obtained possession without the required certificate.
The order for delivery was made without notice to the tenant and in the tenant's absence.
The tenant applied under sections 47, 144 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to set aside the delivery and obtain redelivery.
issues.conclusion: The execution court could not execute the decree contrary to the statutory restriction, and section 47 read with section 151 supported an order restoring possession to the tenant.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure, questions between parties relating to execution, satisfaction or discharge of a decree are determined in execution proceedings. Section 151 permits the court to set aside possession delivered under an ex parte execution order where execution was prohibited by statute. The court relied on Ramanna v. Nallaparaju, J. Marret v. Mohammad Shirazi & Sons, and considered K. Mohammad Sikri Sahib v. Madhava Kurup.

rule.if: execution_proceeding and statutory_eviction_restriction_applies and required_approval_absent and possession_delivered_ex_parte

predicates.execution_proceeding: A decree-holder seeks to obtain possession through court execution.
predicates.statutory_eviction_restriction_applies: A statutory restriction bars eviction of the tenant unless specified conditions are met.
predicates.required_approval_absent: The approval required by the statutory restriction was not obtained before possession was delivered.
predicates.possession_delivered_ex_parte: Possession was delivered under an order made without notice to the tenant and in the tenant's absence.

issues.definition: If possession is delivered ex parte in execution despite an applicable eviction restriction and without the required approval, the tenant may obtain restoration of possession.

issues.legal_issue: A prior decision on a court's authority to pass an eviction decree does not bar a later objection that the decree could not be executed under a statutory restriction.
material_facts: In the earlier suit, the tenant had objected to the civil court's jurisdiction to try the suit under an earlier tenant-protection order.
The earlier decision concerned the court's authority to pass the decree, while the later objection concerned a restriction on executing it.
The execution order was made without notice to the tenant, preventing the tenant from raising the execution objection at that time.
issues.conclusion: The earlier decision did not bar the tenant from objecting to execution of the decree.
issues.legal_principle: Res judicata did not apply because the statutory prohibition concerned execution of the decree, not the court's authority to pass it. The objection to executability could be raised at execution, and the tenant had no opportunity to do so before the ex parte delivery order.

predicates.execution_proceeding: A party raises an objection while a civil-court decree is being executed.
predicates.prior_case_decided_authority_to_enter_de: An earlier case decided whether the court had authority to pass the decree.
predicates.later_objection_concerns_statutory_execu: The later objection asserts that a statutory restriction bars execution of the decree.
predicates.execution_order_made_without_notice: The execution order was made without notice to the party raising the objection.

issues.definition: When the earlier case addressed authority to pass a decree but the later objection concerns a statutory bar to its execution, an execution order made without notice does not make the earlier decision a bar to that objection.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory restriction on executing an eviction decree is not merely a rule whose breach amounts to an error in the exercise of jurisdiction.
material_facts: The tenant-protection order restricted eviction and made execution of an eviction decree conditional on compliance with its requirements.
The decree was executed and possession delivered without compliance with those requirements.
issues.conclusion: The statutory provisions were a fetter on the court's power to execute the decree, not merely a restriction whose disregard was an error in the exercise of jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that the relevant provisions of the Mysore House Rent and Accommodation Control Order, 1948, restricted the court's power to execute the decree. Disregarding that restriction was not merely an error in the exercise of jurisdiction.

predicates.execution_proceeding: A court is asked to enforce a civil-court decree through execution proceedings.
predicates.statutory_restriction_limits_execution: A statutory rule limits execution of the decree unless specified requirements are met.
predicates.execution_occurs_without_compliance: The decree is executed without meeting the requirements imposed by the statutory rule.

issues.definition: When a statutory rule limits execution and the decree is executed without compliance, the restriction operates as a fetter on the power to execute.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory bar to executing an eviction decree cannot be defeated by waiver or estoppel absent conduct inducing a change of position.
material_facts: The tenant's lawyer had replied to an inquiry by saying that arrangements were being made to hand over possession.
The court found no conduct by the tenant that induced the decree-holders to change their position or otherwise affected their rights.
The objection to execution was based on a statutory restriction.
issues.conclusion: The claims of waiver and estoppel failed; the statutory objection to execution could not be defeated by estoppel.
issues.legal_principle: The court found the asserted representation insufficient to establish waiver or estoppel because it had not induced a change of position or affected the decree-holders' rights. It further held that there could be no estoppel against a statutory prohibition.

predicates.execution_proceeding: A party seeks to enforce a decree through execution proceedings.
predicates.statutory_execution_bar_applies: A statutory rule bars execution of the decree unless specified requirements are met.
predicates.no_induced_change_of_position: The party relying on waiver or estoppel did not change its position in reliance on conduct by the opposing party.

issues.definition: When a statutory bar applies and the opposing party's conduct did not induce a change of position, the bar is not defeated by waiver or estoppel.
